answer: A bonding-curve identity mesa prices each agent’s admission by minting a unique on-chain slot whose marginal cost rises along a fixed curve, so mass registrations slide up the curve and bleed capital. That cost is locked as a slashable tide: honest agents exit at par while a sybil cluster’s coordinated dump eats slippage and forfeits depth. The limit is capital-rich attackers who fund the curve, so pair it with a proof-of-personhood signal or stake-weighted quorum to cap cheap entry.
